text:
if a token has a TTL of 15 minutes (900 seconds), and payments-api's clock is 411 seconds behind.
If payments-api's clock is 411 seconds behind, then when it receives a token issued at $T$, its local time is $T - 411$.
The token's `iat` is $T$.
Since local time $T - 411 < T$, the token is "not yet valid" (used before issued) because $T - 411 < T$.
Wait, why didn't this happen for RS256 tokens?
Maybe the RS256 verification in payments-api didn't check `iat`? Or maybe the clock skew only started
